title: Funnel/ROI analytics are not tenant-scoped while calibration on the same page is — demo/sim rows pollute the QBR numbers
expected: Every figure on the Analytics tab aggregates only the current workspace's pipeline, so the numbers Kateřina defends to leadership are her org's numbers.
got: pipelineAnalytics() SELECTs pipeline_entries/pipeline_events with no workspace_id filter (the column + index exist; inserts default 'workspace'), so a demo-workspace simulation run — or any second tenant — lands in the funnel, momentum, automation rollup and ROI. The sibling /api/analytics/calibration route IS scoped via currentWorkspace(), so two panels on one page follow different tenancy rules and their cohorts cannot reconcile. /api/demo documents the seam itself ('~28 unscoped tables') and fail-closes demo minting in gated deploys.
l2_priority: Run the keyless simulation (or mint a demo session in a gated config), then diff /api/analytics before/after: confirm sim/demo entries appear in the funnel counts while the calibration sample size does not move.
suggested_acceptance: Filter pipelineAnalytics (and the momentum/kind-count/source queries it issues) by currentWorkspace(), matching the calibration route, so every panel on the Analytics tab shares one tenant boundary.

title: The new llm_usage spend ledger is only fed by Python-spawned calls — TS-side Gemini (GitHub deep-dive) and voice never meter, so the spend figure understates
expected: The LLM spend/usage ledger (the 2026-06-20 tiger headline gap, now built) covers every paid model call, so the Models usage panel is a truthful total Kateřina can put on the cost side of her ROI slide.
got: llm_usage exists end-to-end (schema, NDJSON sidecar ingest, /api/llm/usage, Models UsagePanel) but is written ONLY by spawnPython's sidecar ingest per the route's own comment. The GitHub deep-dive calls Gemini directly from TS with no metering (grep: no insertLlmUsage/sidecar in the route), and voice interviews (OpenAI Realtime / ElevenLabs) are metered in plan minutes (recordMeterUsage), never costed into llm_usage. An understated cost ledger silently overstates ROI.
l2_priority: Run one GitHub deep-dive live with a key, then read /api/llm/usage: confirm no row lands for the call. Same probe for a voice interview turn.
suggested_acceptance: Meter the TS-side call sites into llm_usage (an insertLlmUsage envelope around the direct GoogleGenAI call; a per-session cost row for voice), or have the usage panel state its coverage boundary explicitly.

title: AI compute cost never reaches the leadership ROI readout — savings are shown without the cost side, so net-ROI ('the AI paid for itself') is uncomputable on-surface
expected: The leadership readout that claims recruiter-hours + CZK saved also carries what the AI itself cost, so the 'paid for itself' slide is defensible line by line.
got: AutomationRoi has no cost field; cost-per-hire counts only recruiter-entered ad-channel spend; the AI's own cost lives as USD rollups on the operator-gated Models tab (requireOperator — open mode passes, a gated deploy's TA manager may not hold the session), unjoined to hires, roles or CZK. A skeptical CFO's first question — 'minus what the tool cost?' — has no on-surface answer.
l2_priority: Confirm live that the ROI readout and its CSV carry no AI-cost line, and whether the Models usage panel is visible to a non-operator internal session in a gated config.
suggested_acceptance: Join aggregateLlmUsage cost (converted to CZK at a stated rate) into the ROI readout as a 'cost of automation' line and into blended cost-per-hire, or surface it beside czkSaved with the same honest-null rules.

title: The same time-to-hire figure is labeled 'average' in the stat cluster and 'medián' in the leadership readout — and it is a mean
expected: A statistic in a leadership-facing readout is labeled as what it is, identically everywhere it appears.
got: avgTimeToHireDays is an arithmetic mean (sum/length of created→Hired durations). The top-right stat labels it via 'daysAvg' (průměr); the UAT-M7 leadership readout labels the identical value 'rdMedian' → 'medián'. One number, two contradictory labels on one page — the exact numbers-don't-reconcile flag a QBR reviewer catches.
l2_priority: Visual confirm both labels render on one screen; then fix is a one-string change (rdMedian → average) or compute a true median.
suggested_acceptance: Relabel rdMedian to 'průměr' (or compute an actual median and label both stats accordingly).

title: Channel spend is a single lifetime figure — windowed views honestly null all cost columns, so quarter-over-quarter cost trending is impossible
expected: Spend can be recorded per period so a windowed view (30/90 days) shows period-true CPA/CPH and the QBR can trend cost.
got: channel_spend stores one lifetime CZK per channel; the code deliberately nulls costPerApplicant/costPerHire in any windowed cohort ('until spend is stored per-period' — its own words) and the UI explains the dash. Honest, but the quarterly cost story Kateřina reports upward cannot be produced.
ceiling: All-time CPA/CPH remain fully attributed and honest; only period-scoped cost reporting is out of reach until spend rows carry a period.
l2_priority: Confirm the windowed view renders '—' with the explanatory note (not a wrong number).
suggested_acceptance: Store spend as (channel, period, amount) rows and compute windowed cost columns from period-matched spend.

title: Calibration outcome is the recruiter's screen disposition (advance/pass), not hire/retention — decision-prediction, honestly labeled, with a self-confirmation risk
expected: Kateřina's calibration question is 'did the 90%-match candidates actually get hired and stay' — an outcome tier beyond the screen decision.
got: calibrationPairs maps disposition('advance'|'pass') to the binary outcome; hold/undecided excluded by design. The UI copy is honest about it ('zda skóre předpovídá rozhodnutí náboráře'). But if recruiters follow the score, the curve partly measures agreement, not predictive validity, and no hire/retention outcome tier exists.
ceiling: Score→screen-decision reliability is genuinely measured; score→hire and score→retention remain unmeasured tiers.
l2_priority: Low priority; at L2 note whether the panel copy makes the proxy nature legible to a non-statistician.
suggested_acceptance: Add a second outcome tier joining analyses to pipeline outcomes (Hired/terminal) so the curve can be recomputed against hire outcomes when N allows.

title: Carried forward (kat-ac-03, 06-19): decision-records copy still says only auto-rejections seal, though seven kinds now do; a stale comment still references the retired auto mode
expected: Copy and comments reflect the chain's real coverage so the audit trail doesn't read thinner than it is.
got: cs blurb ('Každé automatické zamítnutí je zapečetěno…') and the records route comment ('today: the auto-rejections sealed by screen-wave') predate the human accept/reject, reinstate, offer_terms, scorecard and group-eval seals. automation-pass.ts:280-282 still describes an 'auto' mode that :244-249 declares retired.
l2_priority: Confirm the panel visibly lists non-auto_rejected kinds under a blurb that names only rejections.
suggested_acceptance: Update the cs/en blurbs + the route and automation-pass comments to describe all sealed decision kinds and the retired auto mode.

title: STRENGTH / delta — UAT M7 closed both 06-19 majors: measured %-of-manual-baseline framing + one leadership readout with one CSV
expected: A measured time/cost saving against the stated manual baseline, and one leadership-ready readout, per kat-ac-01/kat-ac-02 (both major on 2026-06-19).
got: automationRoi now anchors saved hours per hire against a stated, override-able 42h manual baseline (pctOfManualBaseline, capped 100, null until a hire exists — honest 'pending'), and the AnalyticsTab renders the three-figure leadership readout (time saved % · cost per hire · time to hire) in one dl with one CSV export that leads with those figures. Per-action minutes remain stated estimates (visible in the CSV as 'Min za kus'), the standard counterfactual method, disclosed not hidden.
ceiling: The saving is a grounded counterfactual (real event counts × stated per-action minute estimates), not a stopwatch measurement; and the readout still lacks the AI-cost line (AC-L1-003).
l2_priority: With seeded automation events + at least one hire, confirm the readout renders the % figure, the pending-state honesty without hires, and that the CSV matches the on-screen numbers.
suggested_acceptance: Protect the baseline-relative framing and honest nulls; mark prior kat-ac-01/kat-ac-02 resolved-verified only after this L2 evidence.

title: STRENGTH — calibration is measured from real decided pairs with an honest n≥20 gate and a per-role-family selector; economics null honestly
expected: Confidence presented with a measured basis; under-data states say so; cost figures never divide dishonestly.
got: computeCalibration bins real workspace-scoped (score, disposition) pairs into a 10-bin reliability curve + Brier, calibrated only at n>=20; the panel refuses under-data curves and says how many outcomes are missing; ?roleFamily + a data-driven family dropdown answer per-family accuracy. CPA/CPH null on no-spend/zero-hires/windowed-vs-lifetime instead of fabricating.
ceiling: Outcome is the screen disposition, not hire/retention (AC-L1-006); the curve needs the seeded-outcomes fixture to render at all.
l2_priority: Seed >=20 decided analyses (env.md fixture #3); assert the curve renders from real pairs and the under-data state is honest below the gate.
suggested_acceptance: Never replace the measured curve + gate with a vanity accuracy %.

title: STRENGTH — every number ends in an action: charts deep-link to the exact board cohort, holds link to the Decisions queue, goals set the thresholds the funnel flags
expected: Metrics are actionable — drill-down or an explicit 'so what', never vanity charts.
got: Funnel bars, dwell rows and the bottleneck banner link into the pipeline board pre-filtered (?stage=/?q=) with tab-scoped params cleared so the board opens on exactly that cohort; automation holds link to the Decisions tab; the goals editor persists per-stage conversion + TTH targets that recolor the funnel and the stat pill; role table and ROI ledger export CSV.
ceiling: Drill-down lands on the live board's CURRENT state — a windowed analytics cohort links to a board filtered by stage/title, not by the same time window.
l2_priority: Click one funnel bar and the bottleneck link live; confirm the board opens filtered to the named cohort.
suggested_acceptance: Keep chart→cohort deep links as the pattern for any new analytics panel.

title: The decision chain and decision log are one global, tenant-unscoped store — candidate PII crosses workspace boundaries on the audit surfaces
expected: The audit trail an anonymous or foreign-tenant session can read contains only that tenant's decisions; the sealed chain respects the workspace boundary.
got: decision_records has no workspace column and listDecisionRecords/verifyDecisionChain read globally; /api/decisions/records and the analytics decision log (listPipelineEvents/countPipelineEvents) apply no tenant filter. Candidate labels and rejection rationales are personal data. /api/demo documents the exposure ('~28 unscoped tables') and mitigates by fail-closing demo minting in gated deploys — an honestly named, still-open seam. Correlates SD-L1-010 (screening-decisions walk); the analytics-side aggravation is inconsistency: calibration on the same page IS scoped.
scope_note: Single-operator dev deployments have one tenant in practice — live impact is low TODAY and rises the moment multi-workspace or the public demo is enabled; the demo mint is fail-closed in gated deploys.
l2_priority: In a gated config with demoSessionAllowed, mint a demo session and GET /api/decisions/records + /api/analytics/decisions: confirm whether the real tenant's candidate labels/rationales return.
suggested_acceptance: Add workspace_id to decision_records and pipeline-event reads on the audit surfaces, scoped via currentWorkspace(); keep chain verification per workspace chain.

title: No sealed decision record names the model/version that produced the score being acted on — provenance stops at the policy label
expected: Every headline AI output carries provenance: model/version, inputs, timestamp, authorizing human (Lucie's scored criterion; AI Act system-version traceability).
got: DecisionRecordInput has no model field; policyVersion carries the policy ('screen-wave/bottom{pct}/maxMatch{n}', 'offer', 'manual', the eval source) and inputs carry scores/thresholds/approver — the LLM model+version behind the score is absent from every seal, although the platform knows it (llm_config routing per use case; the llm_usage ledger stores model per call). The per-analysis provenance dossier is evidence-linked but also model-silent. Correlates SD-L1-004 (the human-ratified record also omits the AI recommendation context).
l2_priority: Export a live dossier after a committed wave: confirm no record field identifies the scoring model/version, then confirm the model IS recoverable from llm_config/llm_usage (i.e. the data exists to seal).
suggested_acceptance: Add modelProvider/modelVersion (from the resolved llm_config for the use case) into the sealed inputs of every AI-derived decision record.

title: The 'export dossier' silently truncates at the latest 200 records while the chain verdict counts every row — an audit export that is not the audit trail
expected: The one-click dossier an auditor receives contains the whole chain (or states its bounds and offers pagination).
got: /api/decisions/records passes no limit, so listDecisionRecords returns its default latest 200 (hard max 1000); the panel list and the exported JSON hold at most 200 records while chain.ok/chain.count are computed over ALL rows. Past 200 sealed decisions, the export self-describes as '<N> records verified' over a smaller array, with no pagination and no truncation notice.
l2_priority: Seed >200 sealed records (script the wave), export the dossier, and confirm records.length < chain.count with no warning in the file.
suggested_acceptance: Export the full chain (paged assembly server-side), or embed an explicit truncation marker + total and add a limit/offset contract to the route.

expected: An auditor can scope the dossier to one data subject from the panel, as the copy instructs ('exportujte záznam kandidáta').
got: The route supports ?candidate=<entryId> for the per-subject dossier, but DecisionRecordsPanel fetches unscoped and no other caller passes the param (grep across app/) — a DSAR response is export-everything-and-filter today. Same seam filed as SD-L1-008 from the Decisions-side walk.
l2_priority: Confirm no candidate-scoped entry point exists anywhere live (candidate drawer included), then verify ?candidate= works when hand-typed.
suggested_acceptance: Add a candidate filter (or a per-candidate 'export dossier' action in the drawer) that passes ?candidate= through to the existing route.

title: DecisionLog CSV exports only the loaded (scrolled) rows — a partial file with no truncation marker inside it
expected: An exported log either covers the filtered set completely or the file itself says it is a partial extract.
got: The export maps `items` — the pages fetched so far — by design ('export the rows the recruiter has isolated (the loaded, filtered set)'). The on-screen 'shown X of Y' makes the partiality visible in the UI, but the CSV carries no total/truncation line, so the file circulates as if complete.
ceiling: The sealed DecisionRecordsPanel dossier — not this CSV — is the audit artifact; this log is operational telemetry.
l2_priority: Export after scrolling one page of a >20-row log; confirm the CSV row count equals the loaded rows only.
suggested_acceptance: Either export the full filtered set server-side or append a 'partial: N of M rows' footer line to the CSV.

title: STRENGTH / delta — the unattended auto-reject mode is removed from the code: every adverse action queues for a human, unconditionally (closes lucie-screening-01/-02 and lucie-analytics-01, all major on 2026-06-19)
expected: No candidate is rejected by a solely-automated decision; the candidate disclosure ('nothing adverse is decided automatically') is true under every shipped configuration.
got: automation-pass declares 'AUTO1 RETIRED (UAT M6 / GDPR Art. 22) … the former opt-in auto reject mode is gone': fairness-cleared rejects are queued via setApproval(rejection_review) for a human click; the human route then emails AND seals. Advances/holds/alerts stay autonomous. The 06-19 disclosure contradiction is structurally impossible now.
ceiling: Auto-ADVANCES remain autonomous (a favorable action — defensible under Art. 22, still an automated decision to disclose); L2 must confirm the queue path live before marking the 06-19 findings resolved-verified.
l2_priority: Run an automation pass over a reject-eligible cohort: confirm the reject lands as a queued rejection_review approval (not an applied reject), and that the human click seals + emails.
suggested_acceptance: Pin the no-unattended-adverse-action invariant with a test; mark lucie-screening-01/-02 + lucie-analytics-01 resolved-verified after L2 evidence.

title: STRENGTH — chain coverage now spans auto rejects, human gate decisions, reversals, offers, scorecards, and governance-aware group-eval (advisory vs lead)
expected: The tamper-evident store covers every consequential decision an auditor would inspect, including reversals and the human clicks that ratify AI output.
got: Seals: screen-wave auto_rejected with decisive numbers + approvedBy; human accept/reject at the gate; reinstated (the override reversal — an overturned rejection is no longer an audit hole); offer_terms; human_scorecard; group_eval_lead only when KO passes, group_eval_advisory in committee/eligibility modes so the audit shows the AI informed — not made — the decision.
ceiling: Seals are best-effort (sealDecisionSafe never throws) — a seal failure logs and proceeds, so the chain is complete-in-design, not guaranteed-complete; and records omit model identity (AC-L1-009).
l2_priority: After one human reject + one reinstate live, confirm both records appear in the exported dossier with correct actors.
suggested_acceptance: Protect the coverage; consider surfacing seal failures (console-only today) as an operator alert.

title: STRENGTH — recomputable tamper-evidence, bilingual export without touching the hash (closes lucie-screening-03), and three-state attribution that never defaults accountability to the machine
expected: Integrity is provable, the export is readable by a Czech auditor without weakening the seal, and auto/human attribution is never silently misassigned.
got: Key-sorted canonical JSON + sha256 chain links; verifyDecisionChain re-hashes every row and names the first divergent seq; the panel headlines the verdict badge. The export adds rationaleLocalized rendered from the structured reasonCode+inputs mirror while the hashed English string stays byte-stable. DecisionLog attribution is auto|human|unknown — an unmapped kind renders UNKNOWN and warns in dev.
ceiling: Tamper-EVIDENT, not tamper-proof: a writer with DB access could rebuild the whole chain; the verdict proves internal consistency, not external anchoring (no periodic hash publication).
l2_priority: Flip one byte in a stored payload_json on a scratch DB copy and confirm the panel shows the broken-chain alert at the right seq.
suggested_acceptance: Keep the verify-on-read badge; consider anchoring the head hash externally (log/export) for stronger non-repudiation.
